`route.ts:105–110` selects only the authenticated socket peer or the constant `unstamped`. ## Missing stamps and deployment boundary

The fallback is a **bounded shared bucket**, not immediate HTTP rejection. All unstamped calls share five attempts in one fixed 60-second window; the sixth is 429 even with new XFF values. The first five still perform normal verification, and a correct code can issue a cookie. The new unstamped regression pins that policy and fails on the parent. There is no live unstamped-stamper-disable claim.

Budgets are per exact `socket.remoteAddress` string, not per person or necessarily per browser IP behind a proxy. Direct LAN and loopback addresses have separate budgets, as exercised. **[INFERENCE: documented deployment and source]** Caddy forwarding to loopback makes its remote users share the proxy's socket budget, potentially also sharing with matching direct loopback traffic. IPv4, IPv6 and mapped-IPv4 strings are not normalized. This is the chosen socket-peer policy, not an XFF bypass; do not describe it as per-LAN-client throttling behind Caddy. Counters remain process-local and reset on process restart.
